rv.q: The dialogue is half made up of rhyming couplets that sound straight out of a Latin translation, and half of crude sex jokes and thrown around terms like ‘bitch’ and ‘whore’. While this is a story that could be evergreen, the book is incredibly on the nose with it’s Trumpisms, from ‘aliens’ stealing jobs to cries to 'Make Rome Great Again'.
Structurally unsound, the show needs significant reworking to fashion it into something more coherent.
Its biggest obstacle is discovering its own identity, as right now it veers between two completely different tones that don’t complement each other at all, instead resulting in an uneven watch.
Ultimately, Nero can’t decide whether it is a biting political satire, a psychological tragedy, a crude vaudeville comedy or a no-holds-barred rock musical.
Whatever the answer may be, it surely cannot be Nero: A New Musical.

cn.t: Despite a talented cast and some strong songs, this long-gestating musical about the Roman Emperor emerges as a muddled, tonally confused mess that fails to balance political satire with melodrama.
